title: Computation after lookup: does placement change learned behavior?
question: Does placement change learned behavior when lexical memory capacity is held fixed?
hypothesis: Earlier retrieved values may affect later tokens without improving held-out scores.
failure_interpretation: Equal memory capacity does not imply useful retrieval.
controls: Fix tokenizer, dataset source and packing within each selected data route.
Fix seed-matched model width, depth, heads, optimizer, runtime, budget, evaluator, and endpoint policy unless a listed axis changes.
Report held-out language-model loss separately from each capability card category.
confounders: Model-construction RNG changes when module inventories differ.
Approximate scale classes rather than matched parameter counts.
Educational-kernel overhead is not an architecture-speed measurement.
hardware_notes: Run micro before TinyStories when possible; middle and multiple injection sites are unavailable.
runtime_class: Qualitative scale-dependent educational PyTorch workload; measure local runtime rather than inferring timing.

papers.title: Engram
papers.claim_boundary: Motivates memory questions; SparseLab lexical memory is a local educational implementation, not a reproduction.

can_establish: Controlled observed differences between no memory, final memory, and embedding memory at declared endpoints.
cannot_establish: A speed claim, semantic retrieval result, unseen-fact transfer, or cross-tokenizer equivalence.
prerequisites: Only final and embedding injection are implemented; middle and multiple sites are unavailable.
